A mirror is even by construction, and 540 high-Elo replays give a healthy behavioral read on what separates the winning seat from the losing one. The only low-confidence number is the CDN seat split (64.3% first / 35.7% second) — it comes from just 34 ranked games and should be read as directional.

The mirror is 50% by definition (n=34 CDN ranked games), but the seat may not be: first took 64.3% of that thin sample, inverting Nami's field-wide second-seat lean (56.4% second across 714 games). Across 540 high-Elo replays, winning looks the same from either chair: proc the leader draw every single turn, defend with the +2000 buff plus one small counter instead of stacking raw counters, and shift damage from face to board around turn 5. Going second there is one hard checkpoint: Whitebeard hit the table on the 10-DON turn in 85.3% of 143 wins but only 60.2% of 128 losses.

Gameplan

You are playing against your own 50. Across 3,191 pooled games the consensus lists are identical: 5c Nami x4, Nico Robin x4, Zeus x4, Borsalino x4, Gecko Moria x4, Whitebeard x3, the full Thriller Bark trigger shell (Kumacy, Dr. Hogback, Perona at x4 each, 86-88% presence), and the same flex slots (Teach, Zoro, Kikunojo, Girl). Nobody gets surprised here. The mirror is an execution race across three engines both decks share: the leader draw (13,836 recorded procs in the corpus), the trash-to-+2000 defensive buff, and Moria rebuying whatever the first two engines put in the trash.

The shared script. Both seats want the same spine: Girl early for filtering and DON gifts, 5c Nami on the 5-6 DON turn (61.2% of 134 first-seat wins on turn 3, 60.1% of 143 second-seat wins), Nico Robin on the 7-8 DON turn (67.2% / 71.3%), then Gecko Moria and Whitebeard on 9-10 DON. Early attacks are all face — 97-100% of turn-2 swings and 82-97% of turn-3 swings target the leader, at a 7000 median — then the target mix flips hard: by turn 6 winners aimed only about 30% of attacks at the leader and farmed the board instead.

The resource war is counter-card economics. Every leader swing in this matchup costs the attacker about 2 DON and costs the defender either 1 life or roughly 2 cards. The buff is what bends that exchange: 5000 base + 2000 = 7000 stops any 6000 swing with a single trashed card — and the card you trash is your worst one (Kikunojo was the most-trashed buff fodder in the whole corpus at 1,709 trashes, followed by surplus copies of Whitebeard, Gecko Moria, Dr. Hogback, Perona, Nico Robin). Better: trashed Hogbacks and Peronas are exactly what your Moria rebuys, so the defense literally loads your turn-5 play. Because attacker wins ties, both sides size leader swings at 7000-8000 — a 6000 swing dies to the buff alone, which is why you almost never see one after turn 2. Games average about 8.5 turns and the side whose hand runs dry first loses the last three of them: winning hands held roughly 6.1 cards at turn 5 versus 5.3-5.9 in losses, and that gap is mostly leader-draw discipline (in 134 first-seat wins the draw fired 114 times on turn 4 alone; in 135 first-seat losses, 90).

On the play, you are the aggressor by default. Every power spike lands half a turn earlier: your 5c Nami strips life before theirs, your Robin refills first, your Whitebeard walls first. In won games on the play (n=399), the opponent lost their first life on turn 2 in 60.5% of games and by turn 3 in 93%, while your own life usually held until turn 3-4 — and winning first seats were still at a median 4 life entering turn 5. The one scary moment is their full-DON crackback (a 9000 leader swing on their second turn); the data is unambiguous that you take it — winners spent counter cards on just 3.7% of those swings, losers 10.6%. The CDN seat split (64.3% first, n=34) is thin, but it agrees with the tempo logic: take first when you win the roll.

On the draw, you bank early and wall late. Winning second seats absorbed the early beats — median 3 life (range 2-3) already after turn 3 — while curving Girl turn 1 (41.3% of wins vs 31.2% of losses), Marco turn 2 (25.2%), then pivoted to full defense a turn before the first seat expects it: on turn 4 they took only 15.0% of incoming swings and buffed 86.1% of them. The payoff turn is 10 DON on turn 5: Whitebeard, draw 2, 12000 blocker, and 2 DON gifted onto the leader so every future swing starts at 7000. Missing that drop is the single strongest loss marker in the packet. From turn 7 on, winning second seats countered 58.5% of swings and took just 14.2%.

Both seats converge on the same endgame: blocker walls, 2000-counters, and a take-rate war. Winners kept taking hits at a median 3 life; losers were taking them at 2, which is exactly where two leader swings plus any trigger or Nico Robin KO-burn end the game. The mirror rewards exactly the players who treat hand cards as the real life total — the high-Elo proof: Lamodi#5717 (median Elo ~2193, 11W-3L overall) went 5-0 in this mirror, and dodo3011#1560 (16W-1L overall) went 3-0.

Their threats

Nami OP11-041
Role:

Their leader is the primary attacker all game — 80-100% of incoming swings through turn 3 and still ~30-45% at turns 5-7, most often at exactly 7000.

When:

Every turn from their turn 2 onward; the turn-2 version going second is the full-DON 9000 (or a naked 5000).

Answer:

Math ladder: their 6000 fails to your buffed 7000; their 7000 needs buff + any 1000 counter (8000); their 8000 needs buff + Kumacy (9000). The 9000 turn-2 bomb costs three cards to stop — take it, like 96% of winning first seats did.

Nami (053) EB03-053
Role:

DON ramp plus trigger-free life theft: gifts a rested DON to their leader, then lifts your top life card into your hand while fueling their leader draw.

When:

Their 5-6 DON turn in 50-63% of games across buckets; extra copies appear all game and pitch as 1000-counters late.

Answer:

Zeus KOs it (cost 5 or less) and Gravity Blade bottoms it. Killing it in battle works (6000) but its On K.O. flips a life face-up to free-deploy a 6000-or-less body from their hand — budget for that.

Nico Robin (055) EB03-055
Role:

Net +1 life, an 8000 body, and a deterrent: if you K.O. it on your turn, its owner may burn you for 1.

When:

Their 7-8 DON turn (41-71% across buckets), often again the turn after.

Answer:

Mostly ignore the body — it rarely attacks early. If you must K.O. it, do it while your own leader draw hasn't fired (the burn lands on your turn, so the lost life at least feeds your once-per-turn draw) and never at 1 life.

Edward.Newgate (SP) OP13-042
Role:

The wall: 12000 blocker, draws 2, gifts 2 rested DON each to leader and a character — their leader swings 7000 base forever after.

When:

Turn 5 on the draw (85.3% of their second-seat wins), turn 6 on the play (~75%); it attacks at 12000-14000 in games they win.

Answer:

No clean removal exists in either list — Mr. 3's lock stops at cost 9. Bait the block with a spare attacker so your real swings only face counters, grant Sanji's Unblockable to your closer, or trade your own Whitebeard's block into its 12000 swing.

Gecko Moria OP14-104
Role:

Converts their trash (stocked by buff fodder and 1000-counters) back into a free Dr. Hogback/Perona, or stuffs a face-up card into life; 10000 body that swings 10000-12000 late.

When:

Turn 5 in 33-44% of games, the exact turn their trash is loaded.

Answer:

Mr. 3 attack-locks it (cost 8). Expect a body alongside whatever it rebuys — clear the rebought 4-cost before it starts countering for value as a Kumacy revival target again.

Zeus (SP) OP11-106
Role:

Their cheapest removal — K.O. anything cost 5 or less — and a 2000-counter the rest of the time; the life-to-hand cost even procs their leader draw.

When:

Any turn from 2 onward; assume all 4 copies.

Answer:

Your 5c Nami and Borsalino will die to it — front-load their value (the DON gift and life steal happen On Play, so Zeus eats only the body). Don't sequence a board where one Zeus undoes your whole turn.

Marshall D. Teach OP16-119
Role:

10000 body that banks an extra life from the top 3, and the nastiest trigger in the mirror: strip ALL effects from one of your characters for the rest of the game, then K.O. a 5-cost.

When:

Playable from 8 DON onward; the trigger threatens from their life any time you go face — 81.4% of lists run 2.

Answer:

Nothing prevents the trigger; just know a flipped Teach can permanently blank your Whitebeard's blocker. It is one more reason winners route mid-game damage through 5c Nami steals (no trigger) instead of extra face swings.

Borsalino EB04-058
Role:

6000 blocker that refunds a life when they are at 2 or less — it un-does your last hit exactly when you smell lethal.

When:

Turns 4+ steadily, peaking turns 7-8 (17-29% deploy rates) as a desperation wall.

Answer:

Zeus (cost 5) or Gravity Blade removes it before the swing; otherwise spend a spare attacker to force the block, then send the lethal swing at the leader.

Nami (053) EB03-053

Why:

Trash 1 life, add 2: net +1 life, a leader-draw proc on your own turn, and an 8000 body the opponent does not want to K.O. into. The single most standardized winning play in the data — 67.2% of first-seat wins on turn 4, 71.3% of second-seat wins.

Edward.Newgate (SP) OP13-042
Why:

Kumacy OP14-102
Why:

The number-one counter card in nearly every bucket of the data (e.g., 35 uses on turn 6 alone in 143 second-seat wins). Its 2000 is what turns the buff into an 8000-swing answer: 5000 + 2000 buff + 2000 = 9000. Its trigger also rebuys a Thriller Bark body.

Zeus (SP) OP11-106
Why:

2000-counter, removal, and engine in one card: the life-to-hand cost is a life removal on your turn, so Zeus plays as K.O. a 5-cost, plus the life card to hand, plus a leader draw if your hand stays at 7 or less after the add.

Girl (OP14 Release Event) P-096
Why:

Draw-1-trash-1 filtering plus a once-per-turn rested-DON gift to a [Nami] card — your leader qualifies. This is how winners swing 7000 on turns whose DON all went into a deploy. Turn 1-2 in roughly half of wins (53.7% turn 2 on the play; 41.3% turn 1 on the draw vs 31.2% in losses).

Kikunojo (Reprint) OP06-104

The premier buff fodder — 1,709 corpus trashes, the most of any card — because it has no counter value and its body is replaceable. Late, the body itself converts into a life when it dies with the opponent at 3 or less.

Ship everything 8-cost-plus: Whitebeard and Gecko Moria are 3-4 copies deep, you will draw into them by the 9-10 DON turns, and an opening hand clogged with them is exactly how second seats miss the turn-5 Whitebeard that decides their games.

Resource control

❤️ LIFE

Life in this mirror is a currency with two exchange rates, and the seats price it differently. On your own turn, a life leaving ANYBODY'S life area can pay you a card — Nico Robin's self-trash, Zeus's cost, 5c Nami's steal, or your attacks connecting all proc the leader draw (hand 7 or less). On their turn, lost life pays you nothing but a possible trigger. That asymmetry produces the observed seat scripts: winning first seats hoarded life — median 4 entering turn 5, with the average actually RISING about half a life across the Robin window (3.33 to 3.55, n=399) — while winning second seats sold life early (median 3, range 2-3, after turn 3) to bank hand, then slammed the door (took 15.0% on turn 4, 14.2% by turn 7). The number that actually separates winners from losers is life-when-hit late: winners from both seats were at median 3 when they chose to take from turn 6 on; losers were at 2 (and taking 37-44% of swings there). Treat 2 life as the hard floor: at 2, their Kikunojo and Rayleigh thresholds are armed, Borsalino keeps re-walling, and any flipped trigger plus two swings is lethal. Refill before you cross it — Robin and Zoro add life while drawing you cards, and Borsalino refunds one once you are at 2 or less.

✋ HAND

Both leaders draw an extra card nearly every turn, so the mirror's hand war is about ceilings, floors, and trash quality. Ceiling: the draw needs 7 or less in hand, and winning hand curves prove the discipline — they plateau at 6.6-6.7 around turns 3-4 and never crest 7 from either seat. Sequence every turn so you are at 7 or less BEFORE your first life-removal event: deploy first, steal/swing second. Floor: the losing pattern is a hand that bleeds out by turn 6 — won second-seat games held about 6.1 cards at turn 5 against 5.3 in losses (n=482/409), and the late take-rates follow directly (turn 8: winners took ~23-27%, losers 39-41%). Spend order matters as much as spend rate. The +2000 buff converts your WORST card into 2000 of defense, so trash strictly by the corpus hierarchy: Kikunojo first (1,709 corpus trashes), then surplus Whitebeard/Gecko Moria/Nico Robin copies — never a live 2000-counter. Counter with Dr. Hogback and Perona 1000s early so they stock Moria's rebuy pile, and ration Kumacy/Zeus/Baby 5 2000s for turns 6+ where the common incoming swing sizes stay at 7000-8000 and winners counter 40-58% of everything.

💠 DON!!

The curve is exact-cost almost every turn (5c Nami at 5-6, Nico Robin at 7-8, Whitebeard at 10), so loose DON is rare and gifts do the attacking. Girl's once-per-turn rested-DON gift plus 5c Nami's On Play gift are why observed leader swings stay at 7000 median even on turns where every active DON went into a deploy: 5000 + 1000 + 1000. After Whitebeard's 2-DON gift, the leader swings 7000 base without spending anything, which frees whole turns of DON for double-deploys. Two sizing rules fall straight out of the tie rule (attacker wins ties). Attacking: never send 6000 at their leader — their buff alone (7000) eats it for one trashed card; 7000 is the floor and it forces a two-card answer (buff + 1000), 8000 forces buff + 2000. The data agrees: incoming leader swings cluster at exactly 7000/8000 every turn from 3 on. Defending: you only need 1 DON active to unlock the +2000, so there is no reason to bank more — winning seats dumped everything into board and swing size, and the only 7-cost event in the lists (Gravity Blade, 48.8% presence) is the lone reason to ever hold a big DON cushion past mid-game.

Defense guide — take, counter, or buff?

⚠️ the leader draw is [Your Turn] only — life you lose on their turn pays you nothing. Defense in the mirror is therefore pure card economics: every life you take on their turn is one trigger lottery ticket plus one hand card, and every swing you stop costs trash + counters. The buff is the unit that makes stopping affordable, and it needs 1 DON active plus one trashed card, once per turn.

The math ladder (attacker wins ties): their 6000 — buff alone (7000) stops it, cost: one junk card. Their 7000 — buff + any 1000 (8000), two cards. Their 8000 — buff + Kumacy-class 2000 (9000), two cards. Their 9000 turn-2 bomb — buff + 2000 + 1000, three cards: don't. Their 12000-14000 Whitebeard/Gecko Moria swings — counters can't reach; block or take.

Turn 2 (their full-DON window): going first you face 9000-or-5000; winners countered 3.7% of these and took the bomb at 4 life, buffing only the small versions (the buffed 7000 walls a naked 5000-6000 for free). Going second you face 7000-8000: winners took 55.2%, countered 42.7% — take unless buff + one 1000 cleanly beats a 7000.

Turns 3-5 (the buff regime): winners' buff usage runs 72-86% of defended swings and counter rates climb to 47-57%. Spend 1000s (Dr. Hogback, Perona, 5c Nami extras) and bank the 2000s; the 1000s you pitch are Moria ammo. Going second, turn 4 is the documented pivot: 15.0% take rate in wins. Going first you can stay greedier a turn longer (winners took 39.9% on turn 5 at median 4 life).

Turns 6+ (the wall regime): Whitebeard changes the slope — winning first seats blocked 14.3% of swings on turn 6, 23.9% on 7, 29.9% on 8, 34.1% on 9, and their Whitebeard only loses a block-fight to the mirror's own 12000s. Counter rates in wins hold at 40-58% with buffs at 80-89%, and take rates collapse to 14-24% — always at median 3 life, never 2. The losing buckets show the inverse: take rates climbing through 36-44% at median 2 life as hands empty. If you are choosing between taking at 2 and spending your last two counters, the winners' answer is: you were never supposed to be at 2 with an empty hand — refill earlier (Borsalino, Robin) or block.

Closing the game

🎯 win turns 8-9 (games average ~8.5 turns) against an opponent whose hand you have priced out. Count their stops, not their life: from turn 7 a leader swing at 7000-8000 costs them two cards to stop, so three attacks demand roughly six cards — if they show 4-5, lethal math is already on. Sequence the kill turn in this order. First, 5c Nami steal while they still have 3+ life: trigger-free, un-counterable damage that also draws you a card before you commit attacks. Second, strip or tax walls: Zeus the Borsalino (cost 5), Gravity Blade bottoms two of Marco/Borsalino/5c Nami in one card, and force their Whitebeard to rest on a spare attacker — once it blocks, it is out of the turn. Sanji's Unblockable on your Moria or Whitebeard skips that whole conversation (only ~41% of lists run him; nobody plays around it). Third, swing the leader LAST: it cannot be attack-locked by Perona (cost 6 or less only) and your earlier attacks will have drained the exact counters that beat it. Know what they are holding for the crackback: Kumacy/Zeus 2000s, buff fodder, and a Borsalino to re-wall at 2 life — which is why their last two life are combat-only damage (the 5c Nami steal turns off below 3 life) and why you budget one extra attack for the trigger lottery: the consensus list is 20+ trigger slots deep (Kumacy, Gecko Moria, Dr. Hogback, Perona x4 each at 86-88% presence, plus Teach, Baby 5, Kikunojo). A flipped Moria or Teach on their last life can spawn a blocker-shaped problem mid-lethal. And remember your own engine works during the kill: every connect is a draw, so the crackback you are leaving behind is weaker than it looks.

You are winning when…

  • Going second, Whitebeard is on the table at 10 DON on turn 5 — present in 85.3% of 143 wins vs 60.2% of 128 losses, the strongest single marker in the packet.

  • Your hand is 6+ at turn 5 (winning curves: ~6.1-6.4 cards; losing: 5.3-5.9) and has never touched 8 — meaning the draw gate never closed.

  • From turn 6 on, you are taking hits at 3 life with a blocker ready; winners' median life-when-took was 3 in every late bucket, losers' was 2.

  • Their incoming swings are dropping toward 1 per turn by turns 8-9 (wins faced 0.63-0.93; losses 1.09-1.35) — your board farming worked.

  • You are stealing a life with 5c Nami most cycles while their life sits at 3+, so your draw procs are guaranteed and trigger-free.

  • Your trash holds 2+ Thriller Bark bodies when Gecko Moria comes down — your buffs and 1000-counters were sequenced as Moria ammo.

You are losing when…

  • You spent counter cards on the turn-2 full-DON swing going first — losers countered it 10.6% of the time, winners 3.7%.

  • You hit turn 5 going second without Whitebeard — the 40%-of-losses line.

  • You are taking swings at 2 life from turn 7 on (losers took 36-44% of late swings at median 2 life — the death spiral's signature).

  • Hand below 5 by turn 6 (losing curves: 4.5-5.0 at turn 6 vs 5.2-5.7 in wins) — every future 7000 swing now costs life, not cards.

  • You are facing 2+ swings per turn through turns 5-7 (losses: 2.0-2.2; wins: 1.7-1.9) — their board outlived yours.

  • Their Gecko Moria is looping Dr. Hogback/Perona out of a fat trash while yours has nothing to rebuy.

Top mistakes

❌

Countering the turn-2 full-DON 9000 going first.

Stopping 9000 needs buff + 2000 + 1000 — three cards for one life at 4 life. Winners took it 96% of the time card-free; the 10.6% counter rate belongs to the losing bucket.

❌

Swinging 6000 at their leader after turn 2.

Their buff alone makes 7000, and 6000 < 7000 fails — you fed an attack to one piece of trash fodder. 7000 is the floor (forces buff + 1000); the data shows both sides learned this: observed swings cluster at exactly 7000-8000.

❌

Trashing counter cards to the +2000 buff.

Every Kumacy trashed is a future 9000 defense gone. The corpus fodder hierarchy is unambiguous: Kikunojo (1,709 trashes) and surplus Whitebeard/Moria/Robin copies carry the buff; they have no counter value and two of them get rebought by your own Moria anyway.

❌

Skipping the Nico Robin life-trash because losing life feels bad.

It is net +1 life AND a leader-draw proc on your turn. In won first-seat profiles the average life total RISES across the Robin window (3.33 to 3.55, n=399). Robin is the most standardized winning play in the matchup at 67-71%.

❌

Going face every turn past turn 4.

Winners cut leader-targeting to 30-40% by turns 5-6 (losers 37-48%) because face damage flips their 20+ trigger slots and pays their hand a card on the take, while board kills shrink their swing count — losses faced 2.0-2.2 incoming swings per turn mid-game, wins 1.7-1.9.

❌

Starting your turn at 8 cards and attacking anyway.

The draw gate is hand 7 or less — at 8 the proc fizzles and you wasted the turn's engine cycle. Deploy or buff-trash down to 7 before your first life-removal event, every turn.

❌

Holding Zeus as only a counter when their board has a 5-cost.

Zeus at 6 or less in hand is a three-for-one — K.O. their 5c Nami or Borsalino, the life card to hand, and a leader draw. At exactly 7 in hand the life-add puts you to 8 and the draw gate shuts: count before you play him.

❌

K.O.-ing their Nico Robin in battle at 2 life.

Her On K.O. may burn you for 1 on your own turn. At 4 life with your draw unfired it is nearly free (the burn even procs your draw); at 2 life it hands them half a lethal. Kill her on the turns the refund covers it, or not at all.

Tricks & sequencing

  • Steal before you swing: 5c Nami's life-lift procs your once-per-turn draw with certainty, so you see the extra card BEFORE choosing attack sizes — sequencing it after a countered attack wastes nothing, but sequencing it first plays the turn with better information.

  • Girl's Activate: Main gift targets any [Nami] card — your leader is one. Deploy with everything, then gift a rested DON for a 6000-7000 swing on a 'tapped-out' turn. Stack it with 5c Nami's gift for 7000 on the all-in turn-3 line.

  • Counter with Dr. Hogback and Perona 1000s, trash Kikunojo to the buff: all three hit the trash, and two of them come back via Gecko Moria or a flipped Kumacy/Hogback trigger. Your defense literally builds your turn-5 board.

  • Deploy before you attack when at 8 cards — the leader draw checks hand 7 or less when it fires. Same check after Zeus's life-to-hand cost: at 6 or less he is K.O. + 2 cards; at 7 he is K.O. + 1.

  • Bait their Whitebeard with your most expendable attacker first — a rested-DON'd Dr. Hogback does fine. Once it blocks it is rested for the turn, and your Moria/leader swings face only counters. Sanji's Unblockable grant skips the dance entirely and almost nobody plays around a 1-of in 41% of lists.

  • Swing the leader last on kill turns: Perona only locks attackers of cost 6 or less, so your leader is the one attack they can never pre-empt — and by then your earlier swings drained the 2000s that beat it.

  • Watch for fringe Luffy: in 128 second-seat losses it was 10.4% of turn-4 incoming attacks at 7000-8000 — a Rush body at 6+ DON that punishes a blocker-light keep. If they revealed no blockers by turn 3, hold one extra 2000.

  • If you run Hiyori (30.9% of lists): her swap procs your leader draw on your turn AND lets you tuck a chosen trigger (Kumacy) on top of your life — the next hit you take flips a planned revival instead of a blank.

The CDN cell is thin — 34 ranked games, so the seat split (33.3% first / 50.0% second) rests on cells of roughly 15-19 games — but it points the same direction as Ace's meta-wide profile (41.3% first / 57.5% second across 557 games), and the behavioral base is deep: 798 uploaded replays. Dead even on the numbers — 47.1% for Nami across 34 CDN ranked games — but visibly seat-skewed: 33.3% going first vs 50.0% going second (thin cells, so treat it as a lean, not law). Ace is a 6000-power, 3-life leader who converts your pressure into his cards: with a DON!! parked he draws once per turn when damaged or when his 6000+ power Character is K.O.'d, and once per turn he trashes a card to drop your attacker by 2000 mid-battle. You are the better engine — in won replays Nami's leader drew about three times per game versus roughly 2.2-2.5 in losses — so win the card-flow war, strip his life with Nami before you chip it, and never hand Gol.D.Roger a 0-life board where your own blockers become a lose condition.

Gameplan

Their plan. Ace inverts the usual race math. He has 3 life to your 4, a 6000 leader to your 5000, and two effects that monetize getting hit: the DON!!x1 draw whenever he takes damage or loses a 6000+ power body, and the once-per-turn trash to shave 2000 power off your attacker during the battle. Every life you take pays him a card; every undersized attack pays him a free defense. The shell around him is the Whitebeard package: Garp (99.0% of 2,181 pooled lists), Izo (77.4%) and Moby Dick (88.7%) dig; Marco (99.2%) walls and replaces itself; Jozu (88.5%) bounces your five-drops; Yamato and Otama refuel — and both are live from turn one, because he starts at 3 or less life. The top end is Edward.Newgate (99.4%, modal 4, with 4 copies of I Am Whitebeard!! to cheat him out), Zoro (96.1%), and the closers: Gol.D.Roger in 98.3% of lists and Edward.Newgate (OP16) in 41.3%.

Their clock. He swings the leader on T2 in essentially every game (99-100% of his early attacks are Ace himself) at 6000-9000 depending on seat. Volume ramps from one attack a turn (T2-T3) to roughly two by T5-T6, and quality ramps with it: by your T5-T6 you are facing their Edward.Newgate at 12000-14000 (16-24% of incoming attacks in lost games), Zoro at 9000-11000, and a leader pumped to 8000-9000 behind I Am Whitebeard!! or Zoro. His deck does not out-tempo you early; it out-attritions you late if his life never hits zero.

Your plan. A 3-life leader means three damage plus one lethal turn — and your whole deck shortens that track while lengthening yours. The winners' trade line is identical in both seats: Ace down to about 1.6 average life by your T5 (won-first n=127, won-second n=155) and 0.8-0.9 by T7. In losses he flatlines at 1.0-1.5 from T6 to the end of the game while Yamato, Otama and his leader draw rebuild his hand — half-pressure is the losing line here. Sequence the strip before the chip: Nami's life-steal only works while he has 3 or more life, i.e. before any damage lands, and it denies his damage-draw because it is not damage.

The resource war. Both leaders draw off life leaving the board; yours is better because you control it (your turn, hand 7 or less, and your own life leaving counts too) while his needs a DON!! parked and your cooperation. The replay ledger is stark: summing the per-turn engine counts, winners drew off the leader about 3.0 times per game while spending about 3.1-3.7 cards on the +2000 buff; losers drew 2.2-2.5 times while trashing 3.5-4.2. That one-plus-card swing per game shows up exactly where you expect — hands at T7 were 5.0-5.3 in wins versus 4.4-4.5 in losses. Spend deliberately: take early hits into hand, trash Kikunojo (no counter value, the corpus's most-trashed buff fodder at 1,709 trashes) instead of counters, and do not K.O. his 6000+ power bodies casually — that clause plus Marco's draw-2 means a careless Marco kill hands him three cards.

The tax shapes your targeting. A 7000 leader swing dies to the trash (7000 - 2000 = 5000 < 6000); an 8000 Character swing survives it (6000 ties his leader, and ties favor the attacker). Nico Robin at 8000, Gecko Moria at 10000 and Edward.Newgate at 12000-14000 are tax-proof; your leader is not. Winners' attack mix reflects this: in won first-seat games the share of attacks aimed at his leader fell from 100% on T2 to about 32% by T6 — late attacks go at his board, clearing blockers ahead of lethal and dodging his pumped 8000-9000 defensive leader, which only 10000+ beats through the tax.

Seats. The CDN split (33.3% first, 50.0% second, n=34) matches Ace's meta-wide shape — he is a far better deck going second (57.5% vs 41.3% across 557 games), so the seat you dread is the one where he gets the DON advantage. Going second yourself, the script is forgiving: take his 8000-9000 T2 swing (winners took 91.5% of them), develop every turn, pivot to defense on T4 (take rate 29.7%, counter rate 48.6%, buff usage 73.6% in wins), and land Edward.Newgate on your T5 — 74.2% of winners did — a full cycle before his 10-DON turn. Going first you trade the DON curve for initiative: P-096-into-pressure, his first life gone on your T2, your own life held at a median 4 all the way through T5, Whitebeard on T6 (71.7%). Going first the temptation is to over-defend the early 6000s; resisting it is the single clearest first-seat discriminator in the data.

Their threats

Gol.D.Roger OP09-118
Role:

13000 Rush closer with a kill-switch: while he is on the field, if either player has 0 life when a blocker activates, the Ace player wins on the spot. In 98.3% of lists (modal 2).

When:

8-10 DON, the moment you or he sits at 0-1 life. Notably he never cracks the top-three attacker list on any turn — he appears once, to end the game.

Answer:

Keep your life at 2+ from his 8-DON turn onward (Teach, Borsalino, Nico Robin), and once Ace is at 0 with Roger down, never touch a blocker — defend from hand or win first.

Edward.Newgate (SP) OP13-042
Role:

Their copy of the 12000 blocker: draw 2 on play, hands out 2+2 rested DON, then swings 12000-14000 — 16-25% of incoming attacks from your T5-T6 onward in lost games.

When:

Their 10-DON turn, or earlier off I Am Whitebeard!!.

Answer:

Your own Edward.Newgate blocks the 14000 (the wall dies, the damage doesn't land). Countering through it costs 4+ cards — block or take at 3+ life instead. No clean removal exists at cost 10, so out-race the turn he spends deploying it.

Roronoa Zoro (EB04-007) EB04-007
Role:

+2000 to Ace's leader through your next turn (an 8000 defensive leader) and a once-per-turn self-Rush at Characters if you have an 8000+ power body. Swings 9000-11000, 13-22% of attacks T6-T9.

When:

6+ DON, usually right after you commit Edward.Newgate, Gecko Moria or Teach.

Answer:

After Zoro, leader swings need 10000 to beat tax-plus-pump — shift damage to your big Characters. His Rush hunts your 8000+ bodies: Nico Robin punishes it by dealing 1 damage when she is K.O.'d on his turn.

Jozu OP08-047
Role:

Tempo bounce: returns one of your cost-6-or-less Characters to hand while fielding a 7000 attacker (17.8% of T4 incoming attacks in won-first games).

When:

Their 6+ DON midgame turns.

Answer:

Don't double-commit five-drops into open Jozu mana. Re-play value beats raw stats here — a bounced Nami re-triggers its On Play, a bounced Borsalino refills life again at 2 or less. Rayleigh K.O.s Jozu on sight (7000 base, and the 3-or-less-life condition is permanently on).

Boa Hancock (SP) OP07-051
Role:

Attack-locks one of your non-Luffy Characters until the end of his next turn and bottom-decks a cost-1 (Kumacy, Leo). In 93.1% of lists.

When:

6+ DON, aimed at your lethal-setup turns — typically your fresh Edward.Newgate or Gecko Moria.

Answer:

Locked Characters still block — Whitebeard keeps walling. Keep a second attacker or lean on the leader for the kill turn, and don't bank lethal on exactly one body.

I Am Whitebeard!! ST22-015
Role:

8-DON haymaker: plays their Edward.Newgate from hand, banks a life into hand, and leaves the leader at 8000 for a full turn cycle. 4 copies in 99.4% of lists.

When:

Their 8-10 DON turns — assume it from turn five.

Answer:

Pre-commit your chip damage before the 8000-leader cycle; during it, only Gecko Moria/Teach/your Whitebeard connect through the tax. The event has no counter value, so every copy he holds thins his real defense.

Edward.Newgate OP16-003
Role:

The scarier Newgate: his leader gains +2000 and Double Attack on his turn — every connected leader swing takes 2 of your 4 life. In 41.3% of lists (modal 2).

When:

8+ DON late game.

Answer:

Counter leader swings you would normally take — each stop denies two life — and refill the same turn (Borsalino at 2 or less, Teach). At 2 life a Double Attack connect is game over math.

Yamato OP13-054
Role:

Their refuel engine: draw 2 (live from turn one — he starts at 3 life) plus a rested DON to the leader, on a 6000 body that attacks at 6000-8000 from T4. 93.6% of lists run 4.

When:

Any midgame turn, especially while stabilizing at 1-2 life.

Answer:

This card is why a stalled race loses: he draws himself back in at low life. Zeus and Rayleigh both K.O. it on sight; better, deny the stall entirely — winners had him at 0.8-0.9 average life by T7, not parked at 1.

Nami (053) EB03-053

Your most-played card on the 5-6 DON turn in wins (42.5% of T3 deploys going first, 52.9% going second). Gravity Blade Raging Tiger (Reprint) OP06-058

The K.O.-less answer his draw engine hates: bottom-decking Marco plus Uta/Yamato/Jozu triggers no Marco draw-2 and no Ace K.O.-draw. In about 49% of Nami lists — your cleanest lethal-turn blocker removal (note it cannot touch cost-10 Edward.Newgate or Gol.D.Roger).

Girl (OP14 Release Event) P-096
Why:

The winners' opening play in both seats (43.3% of T2 deploys first, 38.7% of T1 deploys second). The draw-1-trash-1 sculpts your curve, and her Activate:Main donates a rested DON to a [Nami] card — your leader included — which is how winners attacked on 88.2% of second-seat T2s at a 6000 median with zero spare DON.

Girl led every winning opening; Nami is the winners' modal play on the 5-6 DON turn in both seats; going second, Zoro (27.7%) and Kikunojo (23.9%) were the winners' T2. Keep at most one top-end card — Edward.Newgate is your most important single card, but two 8-10 cost cards in the opener is how you arrive at the losers' T7 hand (4.4 cards). Nico Robin is a keep only when the rest of the hand curves into her T4 slot.

Resource control

❤️ LIFE

Ace has 3 life; you have 4 plus a refill package he mostly lacks. The winners' trade lines: going first they held a median 4 life through T5 while driving him from 3.0 to about 1.6 average; going second they gave up the first life immediately (72.9% lost it on his T2, and the take rate on that swing was 91.5%) then stabilized around 2.5-2.7 through the midgame. Losses look different on your side of the ledger, not his — in lost first-seat games your average life was 2.16 by T6 and under 2.0 from T7 while he still held about 1.5. Policy: take freely at 4 and 3 — a taken life is a card into your hand, and his early 6000-9000 swings cost two to three cards to stop — then defend hard from 2 (winners' median life-when-taking from T6 on is 2-3). Refill on a schedule: Zoro and Nico Robin whenever convenient, Teach late, and hold Borsalino until you are at 2 or less — its refill clause is dead at 3+. Hard floor: 2 life once he reaches 8 DON. 98.3% of lists run Gol.D.Roger (Rush, 13000) and 41.3% run Edward.Newgate (OP16) for a Double Attack leader; both punish the 1-life stall you could have refilled out of.

✋ HAND

Your leader draw needs 7 or fewer cards in hand and fires only on your turn — it rewards spending. Winners' hands ran 6.0-6.4 through T2-T5 in both seats and 5.0-5.3 at T7; losers held similar or even bigger midgame hands (6.4-6.5 going second — hoarding, not poverty) and then collapsed to 4.4-4.5 by T7. Summing the per-turn engine counts tells you why: winners banked about three leader draws per game while spending about 3.1-3.7 cards on the +2000 buff; losers drew roughly 2.2-2.5 while trashing 3.5-4.2. That one-plus-card flow gap per game is the matchup. Feed your engine deliberately — Nami's strip, Nico Robin's self-trash, and Zeus/Hiyori life-to-hand all remove a life card on your turn, each one a draw. Trash hierarchy for the buff: Kikunojo first (no counter value; the corpus's #1 fodder at 1,709 trashes), then surplus Zoro copies and extra bombs — never a 2000 counter, and never your only Edward.Newgate before the 10-DON turn. Respect his engine in reverse: every K.O. of his 6000+ power bodies can pay his DON-draw, and Marco adds draw-2 on top — when you must clear, bottom-deck with Gravity Blade Raging Tiger instead of killing.

💠 DON!!

Two DON rules run the matchup. First: park one for the +2000 buff on every one of his attack turns from T4 onward — winners' buff usage ran roughly 45-83% of his swings across T4-T9 — with one scripted exception: his T2 going second, where winners buffed only 14.4% of swings because 7000 cannot stop his 8000-9000 opener. Second: attached DON persists through his turn, so DON spent on offense is defense too. Nami's On Play moves a rested DON to your leader — 6000 base, 8000 buffed; Edward.Newgate's two grants make it 7000 base, 9000 buffed, which blanks his pumped 8000-9000 leader swings entirely. Girl's Activate is the sleeper economy: one rested DON per turn to a [Nami] card means full-board turns still produce a 6000 leader swing — the engine behind winners attacking on 88.2% of second-seat T2s with zero unspent DON. Read his side the same way: one DON left open on his board is the tell that the damage-draw is armed; the -2000 tax costs no DON, so assume it is always on. On lethal turns, route Whitebeard's grants to whatever must clear 8000 through the tax.

Defense guide — take, counter, or buff?

Your toolkit: the leader buff (5000 + 2000 = 7000 for one trashed card), true 2000 counters (Kumacy, Zeus, Baby 5), 1000 counters stapled to bodies (Nami, Dr. Hogback, Perona, Borsalino), and from the Whitebeard turn onward a real blocker. The attacker wins ties, so the price list against his common numbers:

  • 6000 (naked leader, T2-T3): buff alone stops it (7000 > 6000) — one trashed card. Or take it at 4 life.
  • 7000 (leader +1 DON, Jozu): buff + any 1000 = 8000. Two cards.
  • 8000 (pumped leader, his first-seat T2): buff + a 2000 = 9000. Two cards, one a premium counter.
  • 9000 (leader stacked, Zoro): buff + 3000 — three cards. Usually wrong before T6; take it.
  • 12000-14000 (their Edward.Newgate): block with your own Whitebeard or take it. Countering costs four-plus cards.

T2-T3. Going second his T2 arrives at 8000-9000 and winners simply took it: 91.5% take rate, 14.4% buff (n=155 won games). Going first his T2 is usually 6000: winners took 34.1% and buffed 68.3%, while losers buffed 79.2% and took only 21.5% — over-defending at 4 life is the clearest first-seat losing tell in the data. Rule: at 4 life, defend only when one card buys a clean stop.

T4-T5. His swings settle at 7000-8000 and Jozu joins (17.8% of T4 attacks). This is the pivot: in won second-seat games the T4 take rate fell to 29.7% while counters hit 48.6% of swings and buff usage 73.6%. Median life-when-taking is 3 — you are now defending the band between 3 and 2. Spend buff-plus-1000s on his 7000s and keep the 2000s for 8000s.

T6 onward. Volume peaks around two swings a turn and quality spikes: their Whitebeard at 12000-14000, Zoro at 9000-11000, the leader at 8000-9000 behind I Am Whitebeard!!. Your Edward.Newgate changes the math — block rates in won buckets jump from near zero to 17-26% per turn. Stack defenses by price: block the biggest Character swing, buff the leader swing (with attached DON your leader defends at 8000-9000 buffed), take the chip you can afford at 3+.

⚠️ Gol.D.Roger rewires the endgame. While he is on the field and either player has 0 life, activating any blocker — yours included — wins him the game. Once Ace is at 0, which is exactly where you are pushing him, your Edward.Newgate and Borsalino become attack-only statues. Hold hand counters for that final cycle and keep your own life at 2+ so a Rush Roger plus a taxed-up leader swing cannot close from an empty board.

Last: his -2000 tax is an offense problem, not a defense one — it fires on your attacks. It cannot help him when you are defending, so never factor it into your counter math, only into your attack sizing.

Closing the game

You need three damage plus one lethal turn through 1000-2000 counters, a once-per-turn -2000, and up to three blocker bodies (Marco at 6000, Uta — effectively 2 cost once he has a 10000 body — LittleOars Jr. at 8000 only while a big Whitebeard is out, plus their 12000 Edward.Newgate).

The winners' clock says commit: Ace averaged about 1.6 life by your T5 in won games in both seats and 0.8-0.9 by T7; in losses he flatlined at 1.0-1.5 from T6 onward while Yamato, Otama and his leader draw rebuilt him. Once he hits 1, assemble the actual kill rather than chipping to 0 and feeding draws while he holds I Am Whitebeard!! for an 8000-leader cycle.

The kill stack: Gravity Blade Raging Tiger bottoms two of Marco/Uta/Yamato/Jozu with zero K.O. triggers — no Marco draw-2, no Ace K.O.-draw — then attack in tax-bait order: leader at 7000 first (he taxes it into the ground or counters cheap), then the tax-proof bodies — Nico Robin at 8000 (6000 after the trash still ties his 6000 leader), Gecko Moria at 10000, your Edward.Newgate at 14000 — and if he hides behind his own Whitebeard, Sanji makes the big swing Unblockable (a 1-of in about 41% of Nami lists). Force 3000+ of counters per real attack and his hand breaks: his counters are 1000-2000 a card, I Am Whitebeard!! has no counter value, and a 3-4 card hand stops roughly one attack and taxes another.

What he is holding for: your 0-1 life. Gol.D.Roger (98.3% of lists) ends games you thought you were winning, and Edward.Newgate (OP16) (41.3%) turns each leader connect into 2 life. Stay at 2+, keep one blocker-free defense plan for the Roger turn, and close on your schedule, not his.

You are winning when…

  • Ace at 2 or less life by your T4 and around 1.6 by T5 — the winners' trade line in both seats.

  • Going first, your own life is still 4 entering T5 (winners' median; in losses you averaged 2.92 by then).

  • Hand of 6+ through T4-T5 with Edward.Newgate held for the 10-DON turn, not mulched to the buff.

  • Your Whitebeard lands on schedule — T5 going second (74.2% in wins) or T6 going first (71.7%) — and blocks about one attack a turn after.

  • Your leader draw is firing near-every turn (winners banked about three per game; losers 2.2-2.5).

  • He is burning his trash-tax on swings you sized at 8000+ anyway — paying a card for nothing.

You are losing when…

  • Ace stabilizes at 1+ life from T6 onward — in lost games he sat at 1.0-1.5 for the rest of the game while your hand ran dry.

  • Your hand is at about 4.5 by T7 (losers: 4.4-4.5; winners: 5.0-5.3).

  • You burned the +2000 buff on his T2 swings at full life going first (losers buffed 79.2% of those and took only 21.5%).

  • From T6 you face about two attacks a turn with no Edward.Newgate wall down.

  • You are sitting at 0-1 life with his DON at 8+ and Gol.D.Roger unseen — the kill-switch turn is loaded.

  • You K.O.'d Marco and his other 6000+ bodies all game and his hand never got smaller.

Top mistakes

❌

Buffing +2000 into his 8000-9000 T2 swing going second.

7000 loses to 8000 — the trashed card changes nothing. Winners took 91.5% of those swings and buffed just 14.4%; the life card goes to your hand anyway.

❌

Over-defending at 4 life going first.

The clearest first-seat losing tell: losers buffed 79.2% of T2 swings and took only 21.5%; winners took 34.1%. Early defense spends cards to protect a resource you have the most of.

❌

Sizing key attacks at exactly 7000.

His tax turns 7000 into 5000, which loses to his 6000 leader outright. 8000 survives it (6000 ties, and ties favor the attacker) — size real attacks at 8000+, or send 7000s only as deliberate tax-bait.

❌

K.O.ing Marco and other 6000+ power bodies without a plan.

Marco pays him draw-2 and any 6000+ K.O. can trigger his DON-draw — a casual kill hands him up to three cards. Bottom-deck with Gravity Blade Raging Tiger instead, and clear on the lethal turn, not before.

❌

Playing Nami for the strip after you have already chipped him.

The strip requires him at 3 or more life — against a 3-life leader that means before any damage. Played late she is a 6000 body and a DON gift; fine, but plan the strip turn or lose it.

❌

Activating any blocker while Gol.D.Roger is in play and either side is at 0 life.

That is his win condition, printed on the card. With Ace at 0 and Roger down, your Edward.Newgate and Borsalino are not blockers anymore — defend from hand.

❌

Letting your hand sit at 8.

The leader draw gates at 7 or less — every life-removal trigger that hits a full hand is a wasted draw. Deploy or trash down before your strip and self-trash effects fire.

❌

Deploying Borsalino at 3-4 life for tempo.

Its refill clause needs you at 2 or less; played early it is a vanilla 6000 blocker. Winners' Borsalino deploys cluster T6-T8, where it is a wall plus a life — exactly the anti-Roger insurance you need.

Tricks & sequencing

  • Girl's Activate:Main gives a rested DON to a [Nami] card — including your leader. Spend all your DON on board, then tap her for a free 6000 leader swing: that line is how winners attacked on 88.2% of T2s going second with nothing left in the pool.

  • Sequence Nami strip-first: it only works while he is at 3+ life, so fire it before your attacks. The strip is not damage — no Ace damage-draw, no Trigger check — and it procs your leader draw before you size the rest of the turn.

  • Every Kikunojo in your life is a free 6000 body: its Trigger plays it whenever your opponent has 3 or less life — permanently true against Ace — and its on-K.O. life refill is always on for the same reason. Factor that into which hits you take.

  • Zeus is two cards in one: a 2000 counter and an on-play that converts a life into hand (triggering your leader draw) while K.O.ing Marco, Yamato or LittleOars Jr.. Decide each game which mode you are short on before the first one leaves your hand.

  • Rayleigh's condition — opponent at 3 or less life — is permanently satisfied by a 3-life leader. It K.O.s Jozu (7000 base) and Uta on sight; prefer Uta or Yamato targets, since a 4000-base Uta kill feeds him nothing.

  • Gravity Blade Raging Tiger on the lethal turn bottoms Marco plus Uta with zero K.O. triggers — no draw-2, no Ace K.O.-draw, no blockers. It cannot touch cost-10 cards, so their Edward.Newgate still needs Sanji's Unblockable or a 14000 you are happy to have blocked.

  • On your Edward.Newgate turn, route both DON grants to your leader: 7000 base means his 6000-7000 chip swings fail against a single buff (9000), and your counters stay in hand for the Whitebeard-sized attacks.

  • Tax-bait sequencing on big turns: open with the leader at 7000 — he either trashes a card to blank it or lets it through — then send the tax-proof attacks (Nico Robin 8000, Gecko Moria 10000, Whitebeard 14000) into a leader who can no longer discount them.

📎

The CDN cell is 34 games, so 47.1% carries a wide interval and the 33.3%/50.0% seat split rests on roughly 15-19 games per cell — lean on the direction (it matches Ace's 41.3%/57.5% meta-wide seat profile across 557 games), not the digits. The 798 replay games are all-Elo and upload-biased, used here strictly for behavior, never win rate. The packet ships no mulligan table, no won-vs-lost deploy curves, and no attack-decision or search-target data for this pairing — the mulligan section is inferred from winners' early deploys, and per-game engine averages (about three leader draws in wins) are sums of the packet's per-turn counts. A few per-turn swing medians (e.g. 5000 leader swings recorded into a 6000 leader on T3 of won-first games) only make sense as pre-attach or pre-buff records, so treat swing medians as approximate. The packet's text for Ace's defensive effect reads 'give... 2000 power' with the sign stripped; on the printed card it is -2000 to your attacking card, which is the reading used throughout. Finally, his flex slots vary: Edward.Newgate (OP16) (41.3%), LittleOars Jr. (40.7%), Mr. 3 (53.6%) and Curiel (50.8%) are in only about half of lists — scout which package you are against before assuming the Double Attack endgame.

The headline 38.5% comes from only 26 CDN ranked games, and the seat splits (42.9% first / 55.6% second) cannot both sit above the overall figure if every game carried a seat tag - so treat the exact numbers as directional. The direction itself is well corroborated: Lucy posts 54.0% against the whole field (387 games) while Nami's baseline is 52.0% (714 games), and the behavioral claims rest on a healthy 469-game high-Elo replay set with clean, repeated won-vs-lost separation.

Lucy is Nami's worst common matchup on the OP16 ladder: 38.5% in the 26-game CDN sample, against a leader running 54.0% field-wide (387 games). Her leader converts every Event or Stage in hand into +1000 power on offense AND defense with no per-turn cap, so your once-per-turn 7000 wall gets out-scaled, and from T5 Sabo adds free 9000-11000 swings. Across 469 high-Elo replays the losses share one signature: Lucy snowballs to two or three attacks a turn by T6-T7, while wins cap her at about one. The winning minority curves 5c Nami into Nico Robin, cracks Lucy to about 2 life by T3-T4, then turns its attacks onto Cavendish, Bartolomeo and Sabo - and takes the second seat when offered.

Gameplan

Their plan. Lucy is an event-stacked Dressrosa midrange deck whose leader is the whole engine: when attacking or being attacked she may trash any number of Event or Stage cards from hand for +1000 power each, per battle, with no turn cap - and once per turn she draws a card after activating any Event with base cost 3 or more, which Go Ahead and Use &#x27;Em (3-cost, draw 2), And No One Else Can Have It! It's Our Memento of Him (4-cost, draw 2 trash 1 into a free 4-cost body) and Would You Let Me Eat the Flame-Flame Fruit? (7-cost, draw 2 plus Double Attack) all switch on. The consensus list (1,520 pooled games) feeds her: 4x Fire Fist, 4x Just Watch Me, Ace!!!, 4x And No One Else Can Have It! It's Our Memento of Him, 4x Barrier-Barrier Pistol, 3x 2-cost Fire Fist, the Dressrosa Kingdom stage in 92.8% of lists, and eight 1-cost searchers (Viola, Rebecca) to chain it together. Her arc: leader-only aggression on T2-T4 (on T2-T3 her leader is 100% of incoming attacks, 5000-8000 after pitches), Cavendish and Bartolomeo value bodies mid-game, then 4x Sabo - a 9000 blocker with a free event attached - takes over from T5, with one Gol.D.Roger (99.5% of lists) as the closer.

Why it's unfavored. The math problem is defensive card-efficiency plus free attackers. Early she pays dearly: an 8000 leader swing means three pitched events, and you stop it with two cards (buffed 7000 + Kumacy 2000 = 9000). But her character attacks cost her nothing, and that is exactly what the loss data shows: in 124 lost high-Elo games on the play, Nami faced two to three attacks every turn from T6 onward (versus one, occasionally two, in the 95 wins), with Sabo alone making 53.9-66.4% of T7-T9 attacks at 9000-11000. Stopping a single 9000 costs you three cards - 7000 buffed + 2000 + 1000 = 10000, because ties go to the attacker - so the loss pattern is mechanical: wide board, three swings, two-plus cards a turn out of your hand. Losers' hands fell from about 6.2 at T4 to 3.3-3.8 by T9-T10; winners held about four and a half or more.

Your opening: win the race you always win. In 306 uploaded wins on the play, Lucy lost her first life on your T2 in 95.1% of games, and her average life was about 2 by your T3. The engine drives it: every life card removed on your turn - hers from your attacks, or your own paid as a cost to Nico Robin, Zeus or Hiyori - draws you a card while your hand is 7 or less, and the draw fired in 84-93% of T2-T4 turns in won games on the play (73-85% in losses). Curve is the delivery mechanism: Girl on T2 (37.9% of wins on the play), 5c Nami on T3 - the most lopsided stat in the packet, on board in 67.4% of won T3s versus 52.4% of lost - and Nico Robin on T4 (54.7% versus 45.2%). Skipping the curve to hold a defensive hand is how Nami pilots talk themselves into the loss column here.

🗝️ from T5, stop tunneling her face. This is the cleanest behavioral split in the 469 games. On T5-T7, winners on the play aimed only 46.8%, 38.1% and 34.2% of their attacks at Lucy's leader, spending the rest on her board; losers stayed at 53.5%, 45.3% and 42.0%. Same gap on the draw: 36.2% and 33.7% on T5-T6 in wins versus 47.5% and 45.5% in losses. The reason is mechanical. Her leader pitch only ever protects her leader; her board has no counter values at all (Sabo, Bartolomeo, Cavendish, Gol.D.Roger - all blank); and her one true [Counter]-tagged event, Just Watch Me, Ace!!!, only gives a Character -3000 - your 12000 Whitebeard attacking 9000 Sabo still connects at 9000 versus 9000. Character attacks into her board are nearly uncounterable; leader attacks into her face hit the full pitch wall. Clear Cavendish and Bartolomeo, lock or absorb Sabo, and her T6-T7 collapses back to one leader swing your buff already answers.

The resource war. Both leaders trade cards for power, but the trash piles are not symmetric. Hers is mostly spent fuel (4+ Events in trash discounts Just Watch Me, Ace!!!); yours is a second hand - Moria replays Thriller Bark 4-drops, Hogback re-dies into them, and the Kumacy/Perona/Hogback triggers play them straight from life. So pitch recursable, counterless cards to the +2000 (corpus-wide top fodder: Kikunojo, spare Whitebeard and Moria copies, Hogback, Perona, spare Robin) and bank every 2000-counter. You will not empty her hand - the leader draw, the draw-2 events and Cavendish refill it constantly - but every event she pitches on defense cannot pump her kill turn, and every one she pitches attacking is gone from her wall. Drain it with attack volume, not attack size: two 7000 swings tax more of her hand than one 9000.

Seats. Take second when offered. The CDN matchup sample is tiny (n=26) but reads 55.6% on the draw versus 42.9% on the play, and the bigger samples agree directionally: Nami is globally better second (56.4% versus 51.0%, 714 games) and Lucy is weaker first (49.4% versus 58.0%, 387 games). The mechanics back it up. Going second you hit 4 DON on T2 for a real body while her T2 swing is at its strongest - and winners on the draw simply took that pumped 5000-8000 swing 41.7% of the time (losers: 33.6%), banking the life rather than feeding two cards into a three-card pump - then 10 DON on T5 buys Whitebeard, the play made in 45.4% of won games on the draw. Going first your edge is tempo (the 95.1% T2 first-blood rate) but you develop one DON behind her Sabo timing.

The clock. Plan for a long game: average length is 7.8-8.2 player-turns in every bucket. Wins are not fast - they are grinds in which Lucy sits at about 1 life from T6 onward (won-game averages) and takes three to five more turns to actually die. Budget hand and life for T7-T9, build the multi-attack turns that drain her pitches, and treat your own life total as the real clock: the games where Nami hit 2 life by T7 are, almost by definition, the lost buckets.

Their threats

Lucy OP15-002

Leader: every-turn attacker and an uncapped defensive wall - trashes any number of Events/Stages for +1000 each, per battle, and draws off any activated 3+ cost Event.

She is 100% of incoming attacks on T2-T3 (one swing a turn at 5000-8000) and keeps swinging 5000-9000 all game.

Answer:

Buff to 7000 by default - unpitched 5000-6000 swings fail outright, and beating 7000 costs her three cards. On your own turns, attack in ascending size so each connect drains pitches before the big swing arrives.

Sabo OP15-046

7-cost 9000 Blocker that activates a free Dressrosa Event on play; her tank and primary late-game attacker.

From T5. In lost games on the play it made 53.9-66.4% of T7-T9 attacks at 9000-11000; in wins its share stayed at 29-47%.

Answer:

You cannot remove it: Zeus caps at cost 5, Gravity Blade at cost 6, Rayleigh at 7000 base power. Mr. 3 locks it (cost 9 or less cannot attack next turn); Whitebeard kills it in battle (12000, and even through Just Watch Me, Ace!!! it connects at 9000 vs 9000). Answer:

Gravity Blade bottom-decks it through the replacement - bottom-decking is not a K.O. Perona locks it (cost 6 or less). Even a 'failed' Zeus K.O. is fine value: the Event she trashes to save him was +1000 on a future pump.

Cavendish (SP) OP10-045
Role:

4-cost 6000 that draws 2 and trashes 1 every time it attacks - her real card engine on legs.

From T3. In lost games on the play it was already attacking on T3 in 25.0% of games, versus 10.4% in wins.

Kill on sight. Zeus K.O.s it for 2 DON and the life-to-hand cost fires your leader draw; your character swings at it meet almost nothing (her board is counterless, hand counters are Viola 2000 / Rebecca 1000 class). Fire Fist OP15-020
Role:

Her swing event: leader +3000 this turn, one of your Characters gets -8000 until the end of HER next End Phase, with an optional trash-2 to K.O. it at 0 power.

When:

Aimed at Nico Robin (8000 - 8000 = 0) and your other big bodies on her tempo turns; the -8000 lingers through your following turn, inviting free attacks into the debuffed body.

Answer:

Spread must-keep bodies across turns and lean on recursion - Moria rebuys any Thriller Bark 4-drop it kills. If Robin dies to it on Lucy's turn, Robin's On K.O. burns a life; at 1-2 life that text alone often deters the play.

Fire Fist OP05-019
Role:

-4000 to one of your Characters, plus a K.O.-at-0-power rider that switches on once LUCY is at 2 or less life - i.e., exactly after you have done your job.

When:

Mid-to-late game, the moment her life hits 2: anything at 4000 power or less - Kumacy (2000), Zeus (2000), Girl (0) - dies for 2 cost, while Baby 5 at 5000 survives at 1000.

Answer:

From her 2-life mark, stop deploying small utility bodies; hold them in hand as 2000-counters where the card does its real matchup job anyway.

Barrier-Barrier Pistol OP10-060
Role:

Bottom-decks any of your Characters with 6000 power or less - not a K.O., so every On K.O. text is skipped. 96.9% of lists, 4 copies.

When:

T3 onward, typically the turn after you commit a 6000 body; activating it (and the rest of her 3+ cost events) also turns on her leader draw.

Answer:

Treat 5c Nami, Kikunojo and Zoro as On Play value whose body is already spent. Never build a plan around their On K.O. lines in this matchup - Robin at 8000 and Moria at 10000 are your bodies that dodge it.

Gol.D.Roger OP09-118
Role:

10-cost 13000 Rush closer with a trap clause: when you activate a Blocker while EITHER player is at 0 life, Lucy wins the game on the spot.

When:

Her 10-DON turns. Its matchup role is bigger than its attack share - you put Lucy at 0-1 life in most games, which arms the trap against your own Whitebeard, Marco and Borsalino.

Answer:

⚠️ once Roger is in play and any life total reads 0, never activate a blocker - defend with the +2000 and hand counters only. A 13000 swing needs 14000 to stop; usually you take it (from 2+ life) and kill back.

Resource control

❤️ LIFE

Nami's engine runs on life movement during YOUR turn, so life is fuel - but this matchup punishes burning it carelessly. The won-vs-lost curves are stark. Winners on the play averaged 3.9 life as late as T5, actually recovering from 3.6 at T3 to about 3.9 across T4-T5 (Nico Robin netting +1, Kikunojo re-stacking on K.O. - live from T2-T3 since Lucy is already at 3 or less in winning lines). Losers sat at 3.5 on T5, 2.7 on T6, 2.3 on T7 (414 uploaded losses on the play). Median life when winners chose to take a hit: 3-4 through T6, then 2-3. Policy by number: at 4, take anything that is not free to stop; at 3, take singles but stop Would You Let Me Eat the Flame-Flame Fruit?'s Double Attack (8000 taking two life - you need 9000: buff plus one 2000); at 2 you are inside one pumped multi-swing turn of dead, which is where won buckets countered 28-41% of swings and ran the +2000 on up to 88.3% of them (T8, won games on the draw). Borsalino is your floor - at 2 or less it blocks AND re-stacks a life, and its deploy share rises across T6-T9 in every bucket. Moria can stack a Thriller Bark body face-up as a bonus life card. 🎯 enter T6 at 3 or better; the lost buckets' median was 2 by T7 with the bottom quartile at 1, and that is the state her T7-T9 attack volume is built to kill.

✋ HAND

Your hand is the defense budget, and the buckets price it precisely. Everyone draws plenty: the leader draw fired in 84-93% of T2-T4 turns in won games on the play and 73-85% in lost ones - winners fire it more because they curve life-movers, not because they run hotter. Hand size is flat around 6 for winners and losers alike through T5; the fork is spend rate. Winners entered T7 with about five cards and T9 with about four and a half; losers were under five at T7 and bled to 3.3-3.8 by T9-T10, under three by the last turns (306 versus 414 uploaded games on the play; the draw-side pools match). Every extra attack Lucy gets is a card off your stack, which is why hand preservation IS board control in this matchup. Pitch order for the +2000 comes straight from the corpus fodder table: Kikunojo (1,709 pitches across the Nami corpus), spare Whitebeard copies (1,605), spare Moria (1,395), Hogback (1,329), Perona (1,297), spare Robin (1,247) - counterless cards, and the Thriller Bark ones come back via Moria, Hogback and the triggers. Never pitch Zeus, Kumacy or Baby 5: the 2000-counter wall is the only thing that stops her 8000-11000 era at acceptable prices. The 7-or-less hand cap on the leader draw is a non-issue - no bucket averaged above 6.3.

💠 DON!!

Neither deck ramps, so the DON game is allocation, not acceleration. Rule one: the +2000 needs a DON on Nami when Lucy attacks. Attack-attached DON persists through her turn, and Girl's Activate, 5c Nami's On Play and Whitebeard's gift all arm it for free - won buckets used the buff on 60-88% of defended swings, making it your single most-used defensive card. A turn that ends with zero DON on the leader is a turn you volunteered to defend at 5000. Rule two: volume beats size on offense. Your median swing is 6000-7000 in every bucket, and against a wall that scales at exactly 1000 per pitched card, two 7000 attacks tax more of her hand than one 9000 - overkill DON on a single attack buys nothing once she decides to take it. Rule three: the second-seat payoff is the 10-DON T5 - 45.4% of won games on the draw converted it into Whitebeard: a 12000 blocker, two cards of dig, and 4 attached DON that translate to a 7000 leader swing plus permanent buff coverage. Keep 2 DON loose mid-game for Zeus the moment Cavendish or a naked Bartolomeo hits the board, and remember Mr. 3's lock is a free Activate once he is already in play - deploy him on a quiet turn, spend him on her loud one.

Defense guide — take, counter, or buff?

Lucy's offense comes in three regimes, and the won buckets defend each one differently.

T2-T3 - the lone leader, 5000-7000 on the play, 5000-8000 on the draw. Every incoming attack here is Lucy herself (100% of T2-T3 attackers in the first-seat buckets). Buff, don't counter. 5000 + 2000 = 7000: her unpitched 5000 and 6000 swings fail outright, and pushing past 7000 costs her three cards. Won games on the play buffed 84.6% of T2 swings and countered only 5.5% (T3: 72.2% buffed, 14.8% countered), taking the rest at a comfortable 4 life. Going second is the stated exception: her 3-DON T2 arrives pumped, and winners on the draw took it 41.7% of the time versus 33.6% in losses - banking 4 to 3 beats spending two cards into a three-card pump.

T4-T5 - Bartolomeo and Cavendish join, 6000-8000. Now the counters come out: won games on the play countered 35.3% of T4 swings, the matchup peak (top cards: Kumacy at 2000, 11 uses; Zeus at 2000, 10; Perona at 1000, 9). 🗝️ an 8000 leader swing means she pitched three events; buffed 7000 + Kumacy 2000 = 9000 stops it with two cards. Two-for-three is the only attrition exchange you win all game - take it every single time she pumps the leader.

T6-T9 - the Sabo regime, 9000-11000. You cannot wall this profitably: 9000 against buffed 7000 + 2000 = 9000 goes to the attacker, so a genuine stop costs three cards (10000 total). Won buckets therefore took roughly 40-50% of late swings (median life when taking: 3, then 2 at the very end), countered 28-41%, and blocked 4-12% - Marco eating a 9000 is a fine trade since his On K.O. draws 2, and Borsalino blocks then re-stacks a life at 2 or less. The model crunch turn is T8 of won games on the draw: +2000 on 88.3% of swings, 40.6% countered, the rest taken only when not lethal-relevant. Late top counters across won buckets: Zeus 2000, Kumacy 2000, Baby 5 2000, Borsalino 1000.

⚠️ two overrides. Would You Let Me Eat the Flame-Flame Fruit? makes her leader 8000 with Double Attack while drawing her 2 - from 2 life you must show 9000+ (buff plus one 2000-counter), and she can still pitch over that, so bring margin on her 7-DON-plus turns. And once Gol.D.Roger is in play with EITHER life total at 0, activating any Blocker loses you the game immediately - endgame defense is buff and hand counters only, and a 13000 Roger swing is usually taken (from 2+ life) rather than stopped.

Closing the game

Anatomy of the kill: you will have Lucy at about 2 life by T3-T4 in winning lines - her first life falls on your T2 in 95.1% of won games on the play, 83.5% by T3 on the draw - and the last two life cards are the entire fight. 5c Nami's pull only works while she is at 3 or more, so the finish must connect in combat through an uncapped pitch wall, Dressrosa Kingdom (+2000 to her leader or Sabo once a battle for one trashed card), thin hand counters (Viola 2000, Rebecca 1000, Jozu 1000) and a 9000 blocker.

Never swing exact lethal. Every event she holds is +1000 on defense, so 'lethal' into a three-event hand is lethal minus 3000. Build volume turns instead: Whitebeard 12000 + Moria 10000 + Teach 10000 + leader 7000 is four separate battles she must answer at one card per 1000. Bait the Sabo block and the Dressrosa Kingdom rest with your cheapest attack first, then escalate - a rested Sabo also cannot block the follow-ups. The won-game life curves show the shape: Lucy averages about 1 life from T6 while the win actually lands around T8-T9. The kill is a two-turn project - drain pitches on turn one, connect twice on turn two.

🎯 park Nico Robin for the endgame. If Lucy removes her on her own turn - a Sabo attack into her, or Fire Fist's -8000 plus the trash-2 K.O. - Robin's On K.O. deals 1 damage, which at 1-2 life she cannot afford; she ends up playing around an 8000 attacker she dare not touch. While you set up, respect her outs: 2-cost Fire Fist starts K.O.ing your 4000-or-less bodies the moment she hits 2 life, Would You Let Me Eat the Flame-Flame Fruit? threatens a two-life swing back, and Gol.D.Roger turns your blockers into a concede button at 0 life. Keep yourself at 2+ until the turn you actually kill her, hold two real counters for the crackback, and send every spare attack at her board until the math is overwhelming.

You are winning when…

  • Lucy at 2 or less life by the end of your T3 - in won games on the play her first life fell on your T2 95.1% of the time (n=306), and 83.5% by T3 on the draw (n=291).

  • Incoming attacks still capped around one per turn at T6-T7; won buckets faced one, occasionally two, while losses faced two to three.

  • Cavendish and Bartolomeo dead or locked, with half or more of your mid-game attacks pointed at her board instead of her face (winners' at-leader share fell to 34-47% by T6-T7).

  • Five or more cards in hand at T7 - winners averaged about five there and four and a half at T9; losers were under that and falling.

  • Your life at 3+ entering T6 with Whitebeard or Moria deployed (won-bucket median life at T6: 3; lost buckets hit median 2 a turn later with the bottom quartile at 1).

  • 5c Nami landed on T3 and Nico Robin on T4 - the on-curve games are disproportionately the won ones (67.4% and 54.7% play rates in wins on the play versus 52.4% and 45.2% in losses).

You are losing when…

  • Two to three attacks coming in every turn from T6 - the lost-bucket signature and the strongest loss correlate in the 469-game set.

  • Sabo untouched and making over half of her late attacks at 9000-11000 (53.9-66.4% across T7-T9 of lost games on the play).

  • Hand at 4 or less on T7 and trending down - losers averaged under five there and 3.3-3.8 by T9-T10.

  • Your life at 2 on T7 with her board still standing (lost buckets: median 2, bottom quartile 1, while her board swings free).

  • Every leader swing she takes is pumped +2000-3000 and she is still drawing off 3+ cost events - you are feeding the pitch wall instead of draining it.

  • Her trash at 4+ Events (discounted Just Watch Me, Ace!!!) with Gol.D.Roger still unspent and your blockers your only late defense.

Top mistakes

❌

Tunneling her leader from T5 onward.

On the play, winners' share of attacks aimed at Lucy's face fell to 46.8%, 38.1% and 34.2% across T5-T7; losers stayed at 53.5%, 45.3% and 42.0% (same gap on the draw). The uncleared board is exactly why losses face two to three swings a turn by T6 while wins face about one - and her board is counterless, so clearing it is cheap.

❌

Spending 2000-counters on her T2-T3 leader swings.

The buff alone (5000 + 2000 = 7000) beats unpitched 5000-6000; won games on the play countered only 5.5% of T2 swings. Every Kumacy burned early is missing at T6-T8 when the 8000-11000 swings arrive.

❌

Letting Cavendish connect even twice.

Draw 2 trash 1 per attack is her hand staying full for the pitch wall. In lost games on the play it was already attacking on T3 in 25.0% of games versus 10.4% in wins. Zeus removes it for 2 DON and the life-cycle cost fires your leader draw.

❌

Pitching counter cards to the +2000.

The corpus fodder hierarchy exists for a reason: Kikunojo, spare Whitebeard and Moria copies, Hogback, Perona - counterless or recursable through Moria, Hogback and the triggers. Pitch a Zeus or Kumacy and you converted 2000 of future defense into 2000 now, in the matchup where the late counter wall decides the game.

❌

Skipping 5c Nami on T3 to hold a defensive hand.

She IS defense: the rested-DON gift arms the +2000 and the life-pull guarantees the engine fires. 67.4% of won T3s on the play made the play versus 52.4% of lost - the widest play-rate gap in the dataset.

❌

Activating a blocker with Gol.D.Roger in play while either side is at 0 life.

His clause wins Lucy the game instantly. You create the 0-life state in most games by design, so the trap is armed in nearly every endgame - block rates in this matchup never exceed about 12% partly for this reason.

❌

Deploying cheap bodies after Lucy reaches 2 life.

2-cost Fire Fist gains its K.O. rider exactly then: -4000 deletes Kumacy, Zeus or Girl for 2 DON. Those cards are 2000-counters and a draw engine - in hand they still do their jobs; on board they are removal targets.

❌

Calling lethal into a stocked hand.

Her pitch has no cap: three events in hand is +3000 on the defending leader, plus Dressrosa Kingdom for 2000 more and a possible Sabo block. Count her hand, drain it with ascending attacks, and only call lethal when the pitch math says she is actually dead.

Tricks & sequencing

  • Lead your main phase with a life-cost effect - Zeus, Nico Robin, Hiyori or 5c Nami's pull - before attacking: the leader draw fires off that life-card removal even if every attack afterward gets pitched or countered.

  • End every turn with at least 1 DON on Nami. Attack-attached DON persists through her turn and the +2000 requires it; Girl's Activate, 5c Nami's gift and Whitebeard's gift arm it without spending fresh DON. Won buckets ran the buff on 60-88% of defended swings.

  • Attack in ascending order into her leader: every stop costs her pitches at 1000 per card, so by the time Whitebeard's 12000 arrives she has either emptied the wall or takes it.

  • Bait the Sabo block with 5c Nami or Kikunojo before your real attack - a rested Sabo cannot block the follow-ups, and Kiku dying on your turn re-stacks your life while firing nothing of hers.

  • Gravity Blade bottom-decks Bartolomeo straight through his K.O.-replacement (it is not a K.O.) and can take Cavendish with it - the cleanest two-for-one her board offers.

  • Threaten K.O.s you do not need to land: every time she saves Bartolomeo by trashing an Event, her future leader pumps shrink by 1000 and her [Counter] resources thin.

  • The moment Lucy hits 2 life, flip your small bodies from board pieces to hand pieces: Kumacy and Zeus are 2000-counters that 2-cost Fire Fist cannot touch in hand.

  • Luffy is real tech here (6.3-8.4% of won T4-T6 deploys on the play): every Event or Blocker she activates reveals your top life card for +1000 per cost on it, and he carries Rush at 6+ DON - he scales in the one matchup where she always activates both.
