At 8.5% of the ladder this is the most common minor pairing, and with zero uploaded replays the plan below is CDN plus combat math.

Their plan: shave your attack math. Shanks takes -1000 off one of your attackers every turn, Shanks (008) is a 6000 blocker that trashes a card to repeat the trick at -2000 once per turn, Hongo and Ace &amp; Sabo &amp; Luffy stack further -2000/-3000 shaves on your characters, and the 12000 Rush Shanks carries a standing -1000 aura over your whole board. A naked 5000 leader swing is dead on arrival — 5000 - 1000 = 4000 loses to their 5000 leader — so attack at 6000 minimum: 1 DON on Nami every turn (6000 - 1000 = 5000 still wins the tie), and lead with Nami at 6000 or Nico Robin at 8000, both of which connect through the debuff.

⚠️ their removal denies your value, not just your bodies. Benn.Beckman trashes a 6000-or-less character on play — trash is not a KO, so Nami dies without her [On K.O.] rebuy — and Shanks (SP) KOs anything 10000 or less, eating Gecko Moria and Nico Robin. Edward.Newgate at 12000 is the one body they can't answer cleanly; prioritize him. On defense your trash-for-+2000 (5000 + 2000 = 7000) blanks their base 5000 leader, but Shanks (002) puts that leader to 7000 on both turns and the 10000-12000 closers outrange the buff — take the big non-lethal hits, bank your 2000-counters, and grind their 5 life with the leader draw firing every turn you connect.

vs Black/Yellow Sengoku OP16-060 Favored on the play — ~54% CDN (n=24)

CDN read: ~54% across 24 ranked games, with a sharp seat skew — ~67% on the play versus ~46% on the draw (n=24, directional only). Presence 6.0%. The tempo gap is the matchup: this deck spends its early turns doing nothing to your life total.

Their plan: durdle, fix DON, and assemble a hand — Sengoku draws 2 and trashes 2, &quot;Buddha&quot; Sengoku and Marineford dig, Koby stacks an extra Navy card onto their life — all building to the leader's haymaker: return 8 DON and deploy up to three different 8000-power Admirals (Kuzan, Sakazuki, Borsalino) in a single turn. 🎯 have the game decided before that turn is online. Their early defense is structurally thin: Three Admirals!'s +4000 counter mode only works with an Admiral in play — mostly a brick until the dump — and Slow-Slow Beam Sword returns a DON to counter, fighting their own 8-DON requirement. Meanwhile your 5000 leader wins the tie into their 5000 leader every turn with no DON support, Nami peels the Koby-stacked card back off their life while cashing your leader draw, and Roronoa Zoro / Nico Robin keep your own life count ahead of the race.

⚠️ Sakazuki's on-play -6000 turns Nico Robin into a 2000 body for a free battle KO (small consolation: KO'd on their turn she burns them for 1), and Kuzan strips [Blocker] from Marco or Borsalino exactly when you need the wall. If the Admiral turn does land, three 8000s outrange your buffed 7000 — pair the buff with a 2000-counter (7000 + 2000 = 9000 > 8000) or just take and keep racing: they returned 8 DON to make that board, so the follow-up swings come with almost nothing behind them.

vs Yellow Luffy & Ace ST30-001 Heavily favored — 75% CDN (n=16)

CDN read: 75% across 16 ranked games — 80% going first, ~88% going second. Small sample, but favored from both seats, and at 6.6% presence you'll queue into it regularly. Your best minor matchup.

Why their gimmick fails against you: the leader gives every Ace- and Luffy-named card +3000 on your turn, turning their 6000 rushers into 9000 defensive walls — a tax on decks that fight boards, which Nami never does. On their own turn the buff is off: Monkey.D.Luffy, Portgas.D.Ace and Monkey.D.Luffy rush in at a naked 6000, and with 1 DON banked on Nami one trashed card makes her 5000 + 2000 = 7000 — the 012/007 swings fail after they already spent a card deploying the attacker, while Monkey.D.Luffy's [When Attacking] can feed itself a rested DON to swing 7000 and win the tie, so stop that one with the buff plus any 1000-counter (7000 + 1000 = 8000). Worse for them, those rush bodies print no counter value at all, so a hand full of attackers defends terribly against your race. The leader itself never gets the +3000 (it buffs only cards named Ace or Luffy, not "Luffy & Ace") and defends at a flat 6000: Nami connects on the winning 6000 tie, Nico Robin is clean at 8000, and your leader needs just 1 DON.

🗝️ never swing into a 9000 wall — every attack at the 4-life leader, the once-per-turn buff on their biggest undonned rush swing, and let the Gecko Moria / Nico Robin life engine stretch a race they can't win long. Watch for Trafalgar Law (SP) growing a blocker once they fall to 1 life, Electrical Luna (about 39% of 885 pooled lists) freezing your rested board for a turn, and Portgas.D.Ace (118) restocking their hand. None of it changes the race math.

vs Blue/Purple Luffy OP11-040 Even to slightly unfavored — 45% CDN (n=20)

CDN read: 45% across 20 ranked games; the going-second subset ran hot (~67%) but at this n the splits are noise — treat it as even-to-slightly-behind. Presence 4.2%, no replay buckets, so this is CDN plus mechanics.

Their plan: ramp into a 6000-power leader grind. Mr.2.Bon.Kurei and It&#x27;s to Die For accelerate DON, the leader's free search switches on at 8 DON, and the payoff is Sanji — a 9-cost 9000 that flips the top card and plays Charlotte Linlin or Gol.D.Roger for free. Nami draws 3 stapled to a blocker, and Gum-Gum Giant defines their defense: 2 DON plus a trashed card for +4000 and draw 2, refueling as they block your race. The 6000 leader is a standing tax — your leader needs 1 DON every single turn just to win the 6000 tie, while their undonned 6000 swings die to your trash-for-7000.

🎯 close before the Sanji turn. Their early board is searchers and ramp with almost no pressure, so force the race with Nami (life strip plus a leader draw on your own turn) and make them burn Gum-Gum Giant DON defensively instead of ramping. ⚠️ Gravity Blade Raging Tiger bottom-decks two of your cost-6-or-less characters with no KO — Nami, Dr. Hogback and Perona vanish with no [On K.O.] value and nothing left in the trash to rebuy (Nico Robin at 7 cost is out of range). Boa Hancock (SP) attack-locks your best body, and a parked 8000 Nico Robin hands Mr.2.Bon.Kurei an 8000 swing via its power-copy. With Gol.D.Roger down their leader defends at 8000 for two turns (your leader and Nami stop connecting; Nico Robin ties through at 8000, and Gecko Moria at 10000 / Edward.Newgate at 12000 still clear it) — the longer it runs the worse your math, so spend life and hand freely to end it by T6.

vs Yellow Sky Luffy OP15-098 Sample too thin to call — 60% CDN (n=5); richest replay map in the chapter

CDN read: only 5 ranked games reached the CDN (60%) — far too thin to call a win rate, and at 1.2% presence you'll rarely see it. But 927 uploaded replays make this the best-mapped behavior file among the minors, and the winning line is remarkably consistent.

Their plan: a pure face race on a life-recycling chassis. Roronoa Zoro and Gum-Gum Golden Rifle keep restocking their life while Monkey.D.Luffy (Rush at 6+ DON, swinging 7000-8000) and Nico Robin apply pressure, with Enel (SP) arriving late at 11000-12000 (about a fifth of T9 incoming attacks in your won games going first). They commit everything to your face — in 385 won games going first, their T2 attack targeted your leader ~98% of the time, either a naked 5000 or pumped to 9000 — and Kalgara mirrors your own engine, drawing them a card the first time a life card moves on their turn (their effect-draws then lock for the rest of the turn). Wyper's -2000 sweep clears your Girl and Zeus (SP) as a bonus.

How winners played it (replay behavior, not a win rate): in those 385 wins going first, pilots held a median 4 life through T4, landed Nami on T3 in 69% of games and Nico Robin on T4 in 48%, then Gecko Moria / Edward.Newgate on T5-6. Defense ran through the leader, not the board: the +2000 buff fired on 76% of defended T2 swings and 88% on T3, while block rates sat at 0-2% all the way through T5. 🗝️ that buff-first pattern is mechanically correct here — Monkey.D.Luffy gains +1000 per cost of a flipped life card every time you activate an Event or a [Blocker], and Nami's leader buff plus raw hand counters are neither, so trash-for-7000 plus a 1000-counter beats his 7000 swings (7000 + 1000 = 8000 > 7000) without feeding the pump — find 2000 more against his 8000 swings; save Marco / Borsalino for attackers that aren't him. In 257 wins going second the midgame is a counter war — 2-3 leader swings a turn on T5-6, with winners countering ~38-41% of them, buffing on 71-82% of defenses, and still holding median 3 life at T6; counter usage was visibly stockpiled early (16.5% of T2 defenses, 29.3% T3) and spent from T5 on. One last freebie: when their leader saves a 6000+ Sky Island body by cashing a life card to hand on your turn, that removed life card triggers your leader draw.

vs Green Mihawk OP14-020 Heavily unfavored — ~22% CDN (n=9, thin)

CDN read: ~22% across just 9 ranked games (25% from either seat) — the worst number on the sheet, though n=9 is too thin to bank, and at 2.6% presence it's mercifully rare. The 748 uploaded replays can't fix the win rate, but they show exactly how the wins happen.

Their plan: rest-and-freeze control behind the deepest counter wall you'll face. The leader untaps 3 extra DON a turn once any 5-cost-or-more character is in play (against Nami it stays 5000 — its +1000 only fires into Slash leaders), funding Demon Aura Nine Sword Style and I Know You&#x27;re Strong... — 1-cost events where the former rests your board, the latter freezes your rested bodies, and both counter for +3000 — plus Trichiliocosm at +2000, or +4000 once they have 8 rested cards. Everything you attack with stays rested and frozen (Jewelry Bonney, Law &amp; Bepo), Perona locks two of your cost-5-or-less characters out of attacking entirely, and the closers outrange your kit: Law &amp; Bepo swings 11000-12000 and Dracule Mihawk 10000-11000 while packing its own defensive trash-for-+2000. The math is brutal — 5000 + 2000 = 7000 against an 11000 swing still demands another 5000 of counters, at usually 1-2 leader swings a turn through the midgame.

How winners survived (replay behavior, not a win rate): in 130 wins going second, pilots treated early life as currency — they took 55% of T3 swings and buffed only 21% — then flipped from T4 on, countering 40-43% of swings with the buff up on ~74% of defenses. In 139 wins going first the arc matches (80% buff usage and 45% countered on T5 defenses), with Edward.Newgate landing on T6 in 49% of wins and block rates climbing from ~2% early to 16.5% by T8 — late, Whitebeard blocking an 11000 is a one-card answer where countering it costs three. ⚠️ Smoker (about half their lists) carries [Banish] — its life damage trashes the card without the [Trigger], blanking your Gecko Moria / Dr. Hogback / Perona trigger package — so never count on life triggers when Smoker is the attacker. The grind line: keep Nami's on-play strip and Nico Robin / Roronoa Zoro life-stacking running so the first life card that moves on your turn cashes the leader draw — Nami's strip and Robin's life-trash both count, while Zoro's stack only adds life and doesn't trigger it — and make their frozen-board turns pay full counter price.

Methodology. Win rates and matchup verdicts come from the matchmaking service's aggregate stats layer (every ranked game; "CDN"). Turn-by-turn behavior (life, take/counter/+2000 rates, deploys, attack patterns) comes from 16,276 parsed replay action-logs of Nami games, split by result and seat; replay win-rates are upload-biased and are never used as matchup verdicts. Card text from the official card database; cross-checked against in-sim observed behavior. Hover or tap any card name to see the card and its effect.
